reviews.text: I witnessed the groomer completely severing the nerves in the dog's claws, and they didn't apologize at all. I felt it was a form of grooming that was close to animal cruelty.
Thank you for your continued support.

They're not considering the animals' feelings at all.

They're confined to small cages and are under extreme stress.

I wouldn't even give it one star; it's so awful, I've never seen a pet shop like this before.

The dogs and cats were crammed into cages so small they could barely walk a few steps. All the animals looked exhausted, the staff were unfriendly, and it was unbearable to watch.

I've only ever owned dogs and cats, so I don't know about the conditions of the other animals, but the birds were tethered by their feet and outside, like a spectacle.

Moreover, all the animals were quite old. It's heartbreaking and sad to see animals forced to live in such terrible conditions, and to know I can't help them.

I was shocked that a pet shop like this even exists. It was too painful to stay, so I left the store.

Unbelievable. I hope it goes out of business.

When I visited the neighboring "Karaage Specialty Shop Kimisei," I noticed an owl in the shop window and decided to go inside.

Inside, there was a black Labrador, a Shiba Inu, a large white dog, a green parakeet, rabbits, and even goldfish—it was truly a "ZOO," just as the shop's name suggests.

The dogs were all very friendly and incredibly cute, and the owl that caught my eye was very gentle and calming.
They gave me a thorough explanation of the product I was looking for. The shop dog was also very well-behaved and cute!

I just moved to Japan, and it broke my heart seeing kittens and puppies in such small cages. No toys, nothing to do all day. I’m surprised such a place is able to exist in Japan in this day and age. This shouldn’t be allowed. Those poor animals :(

I had some time, so I dropped in.
I was greeted by Momon, a young Samoyed, and Kurobee, a mixed breed.
They were free-roaming and playing freely.
Just watching them made me feel warm and fuzzy.
They would come over whenever they felt like it, so I gave them a little petting.
The staff at this zoo are also nice, and the dogs love them too.
I was able to take my time looking at the cute dogs in the zoo.
Thank you very much.
I'd like to visit again.

The animal there don’t seem to be happy. They are not loved. The space for each animal is small and the toilet is always dirty. They don’t have enough food. They look eager to be adopted. It’s a sin to brutally breed and sell animal like this!
Why is there a chained owl? Or a dog with an enclosure that is twice the size of his body? Japan is 50 years behind in terms of animal welfare. Terrible!

I was shocked by how poorly they managed the store. I bought a gecko, but it was having trouble shedding and refusing to eat. The female employee casually said something like, "This one's shedding right now!" It was extremely thin, and its bones were faintly visible. It wouldn't eat crickets, so I force-fed it leopard gecko food mixed with yogurt, but despite my best efforts, it passed away a week after I bought it. I think it must have been in a very desperate state. I'm just furious with this store. Geckos are supposed to be long-lived creatures, so I don't know how they could end up in such a state.
There's been an owl in a visible location for over five years. It's cute.

The Hahns Macaw in the window was wearing a leg harness. Leg harnesses on parrots almost always result in severe injury. Says pretty much everything that needs to be said about the conditions and welfare in this shop.

The display case is way too small!

A cat that's about a year old is kept in a cage that's too narrow in both height and width, and whenever I visit, it's always still and quiet, looking so cramped and pitiful. Cats usually run around after doing their business, right? Would that even be possible in the current cage...?

The person I went with also sadly murmured, "It looks like it's given up..."

It's not just the cat; I think the dogs, birds, chinchillas, and everything else are all too cramped.

Regarding the parakeet, I was told its wings have been clipped so it can't fly...
For some reason, every animal seems to be desperately pleading, "Let me out!"

While being in a cage itself doesn't leave a good impression, the entire facility should be made larger, or if cages are necessary, the environment should be made as comfortable as possible for the animals.

They are living beings, after all.

Thank you for your consideration.
It's heartbreaking to see pets crammed into tiny cages. The conditions are so poor it makes me anxious.
